Earthquakes across the Americas, in orde.Port Royal, Jamaica: Much of this Jamaican pirate haven slid into the sea in 1692. Divers still find streets and buildings under the harbor water.
Earthquakes across the Americas, in orde.New Madrid, Missouri: A series of quakes in 1811 and 1812 shook the Midwest so hard that church bells reportedly rang as far away as Boston.
Earthquakes across the Americas, in orde.Charleston, South Carolina: One of the strongest ever recorded in the eastern United States, this 1886 quake was felt from Cuba to Canada.
Earthquakes across the Americas, in orde.Valparaíso, Chile: Valparaíso's 1906 earthquake wrecked this key Pacific port. The city later rebuilt, and its hillside neighborhoods are a World Heritage site.
Earthquakes across the Americas, in orde.Chillán, Chile: The deadliest quake in Chilean history killed roughly 28,000 and led the government to create a development agency, CORFO, to rebuild the country.
Earthquakes across the Americas, in orde.Ancash, Peru: A landslide set off by this quake buried the town of Yungay, killing about 20,000 people in minutes. Some 70,000 died in all.
Earthquakes across the Americas, in orde.Managua, Nicaragua: This 1972 Christmas-season quake flattened the capital's center. Baseball star Roberto Clemente died flying relief supplies to the city.
Earthquakes across the Americas, in orde.Guatemala: On February 4, 1976, a magnitude 7.5 quake struck the country, killing around 23,000 people. Many lived in adobe homes that collapsed.
Earthquakes across the Americas, in orde.Mexico City: Mexico City sits on an old lakebed, whose soft soil amplified the shaking of the 1985 quake and brought down buildings far from the epicenter.
Earthquakes across the Americas, in orde.Ecuador: A magnitude 7.8 quake in April 2016 hit Ecuador's coast near Pedernales, killing roughly 670 people and damaging many coastal towns.

Toy brands, by debut year.Crayola crayons: The name blends the French 'craie' (chalk) and 'oleaginous', coined by Alice Stead Binney.
Toy brands, by debut year.Hasbro: Founded in Rhode Island by the Hassenfeld brothers, selling fabric remnants before pencil cases.
Toy brands, by debut year.Fisher-Price: Pull toys like the Chatter Telephone and Little People made its name.
Toy brands, by debut year.LEGO: A brick made in 1958 still clicks with ones made today.
Toy brands, by debut year.Mattel: Founded in a garage; the name merges Harold Matson and Elliot Handler, and it made Barbie.
Toy brands, by debut year.Play-Doh: Originally sold as a wallpaper cleaner, it was repurposed as a modelling compound.
Toy brands, by debut year.Hot Wheels: Mattel's answer to Matchbox, with low-friction wheels, its rarest cars are prized by collectors.
Toy brands, by debut year.Playmobil: The German toy figures are 7.5 cm tall, and they debuted in 1974.
Toy brands, by debut year.Beanie Babies: Ty Warner's under-stuffed toys became a 1990s craze.
Toy brands, by debut year.Funko: Founded to sell nostalgia toys, it is known for its Pop! vinyl bobbleheads.

Big volcanic blasts across deep time.Yellowstone (Lava Creek): Around 640,000 years ago the Yellowstone caldera erupted, and its ash blanketed much of North America; it is the most recent of its three giant eruptions.
Big volcanic blasts across deep time.Toba supereruption: The Toba eruption in Sumatra was among the largest in two million years, and some scientists think it cooled the planet for years.
Big volcanic blasts across deep time.Mount Mazama (Crater Lake): Mount Mazama blew apart, and its collapsed caldera filled with rain and snow to become Crater Lake, the deepest lake in the United States.
Big volcanic blasts across deep time.Thera, Santorini: The Minoan eruption of Santorini devastated the island, and some believe it contributed to the decline of the Minoan civilization on Crete.
Big volcanic blasts across deep time.Vesuvius (Pompeii): Vesuvius buried Pompeii and Herculaneum in ash, which preserved loaves of bread, graffiti and even the shapes of victims.
Big volcanic blasts across deep time.Taupō (Hatepe): The Hatepe eruption in New Zealand is one of the biggest of the last 5,000 years, and it left ash layers across the North Island.
Big volcanic blasts across deep time.Huaynaputina, Peru: Huaynaputina is South America's largest historical eruption, and its ash probably contributed to a cold, famine-struck year in Russia.
Big volcanic blasts across deep time.Laki, Iceland: Laki released toxic gas over Europe in 1783, and the resulting haze killed livestock and caused famine in Iceland.
Big volcanic blasts across deep time.Tambora: Tambora's 1815 blast was the largest in recorded history, and 1816 became the Year Without a Summer, with snow in June in New England.
Big volcanic blasts across deep time.Pinatubo: Pinatubo's 1991 eruption in the Philippines cooled the Earth by roughly half a degree Celsius for about a year, and timely evacuation saved thousands.

Which plants came first?.Cyanobacteria: Cyanobacteria are the pond scum that taught Earth to breathe: their photosynthesis filled the atmosphere with oxygen over billions of years.
Which plants came first?.Green algae: Green algae are the ancestors of all land plants, and their descendants today include seaweed-like relatives found in ponds worldwide.
Which plants came first?.First land plants: The first land plants resembled tiny mosses, and they lacked roots, which slowly began turning rock into soil.
Which plants came first?.First vascular plants: Vascular plants developed tubes to carry water and sugars, which let them grow upright and taller than their low, mossy ancestors.
Which plants came first?.First forests: The first forests were made of tree-like Archaeopteris, which had true wood and leaves, and they changed rivers and the climate.
Which plants came first?.Conifers: Conifers like pines and spruces dominated much of the Mesozoic, and they also include some of the tallest and oldest living trees.
Which plants came first?.Ginkgo relatives: Ginkgo is a living fossil whose lineage reaches back hundreds of millions of years, and a ginkgo survived the Hiroshima bomb.
Which plants came first?.Flowering plants: Flowering plants appeared in the dinosaur era and Darwin called their sudden rise in the fossil record an abominable mystery.
Which plants came first?.Grasses: Grasses came late, yet now cover vast areas of Earth, and they feed us as wheat, rice, corn and sugar cane.
Which plants came first?.Cacti: Cacti are native to the Americas, and their spiny, water-storing shape is an adaptation to dry desert life that arose late in plant history.

Pencil grades, by hardness.9H: 9H is the hardest standard grade, producing very pale, thin lines, and is used for technical work where precision matters more than darkness.
Pencil grades, by hardness.4H: 4H leaves light, crisp lines, which makes it popular with draftsmen and architects who need exact lines that do not smudge.
Pencil grades, by hardness.2H: 2H is a common hard pencil for sketching light guidelines that can later be erased or covered over.
Pencil grades, by hardness.H: H sits at the edge of the hard side of the scale, and the letter simply stands for hardness.
Pencil grades, by hardness.F: F is said to stand for fine point, and it holds a sharp tip well, falling between the hard and soft ranges.
Pencil grades, by hardness.HB: HB is the middle of the scale and the classic school pencil, close to the number 2 pencil used in the United States.
Pencil grades, by hardness.B: B stands for black, and it leaves a softer, darker line, which is why artists like it for shading.
Pencil grades, by hardness.2B: 2B is a favorite for sketching, because it has enough softness to create smooth tones without being messy.
Pencil grades, by hardness.4B: 4B gives deep, rich blacks and smudges easily, which is useful for artists who blend with a finger.
Pencil grades, by hardness.8B: 8B is one of the softest, producing velvety dark lines, and artists use it for dramatic shadows.

Milestones in American history.Mayflower lands: Aiming for Virginia, the ship with 102 passengers landed far to the north, at Cape Cod, so its passengers wrote the Mayflower Compact.
Milestones in American history.Salem witch trials: Nineteen people were executed, mostly by hanging, and none were burned; one man was pressed to death with stones for refusing to plead.
Milestones in American history.Boston Tea Party: Colonists disguised as Mohawk men dumped 342 chests of East India Company tea into Boston Harbor to protest taxation without representation.
Milestones in American history.Louisiana Purchase: The US bought about 828,000 square miles from France for roughly 15 million dollars, which doubled the young nation's size.
Milestones in American history.Civil War begins: Confederate forces fired on Fort Sumter in Charleston Harbor, and amazingly no one was killed in the bombardment itself.
Milestones in American history.Statue of Liberty dedicated: France gave the statue, and its pedestal was paid for partly by a newspaper fundraiser led by Joseph Pulitzer; the inscription includes Emma Lazarus's poem.
Milestones in American history.Prohibition begins: The 18th Amendment banned alcohol sales, and it led to speakeasies, bootlegging and a boom in organized crime until it was repealed in 1933.
Milestones in American history.Pearl Harbor attack: The surprise Japanese raid on Hawaii killed over 2,400 Americans and brought the United States into World War II the next day.
Milestones in American history.Watergate break-in: Five men were caught at the Democratic headquarters, and the cover-up that followed forced President Nixon's resignation in 1974.
Milestones in American history.Hurricane Katrina: The storm flooded about 80 percent of New Orleans after its levees failed, and killed over 1,300 people along the Gulf Coast.

Chess ratings: titles and peaks.Woman Candidate Master: Women's titles are separate from the open ones, though top women also earn open titles, as Judit Polgar did without ever playing women's events.
Chess ratings: titles and peaks.Woman FIDE Master: One step above the WCM, though many top women skip these and go straight for the open Grandmaster title.
Chess ratings: titles and peaks.Candidate Master: Awarded for reaching a 2200 rating, with no tournament norms needed, so it is the first title many serious club players earn.
Chess ratings: titles and peaks.FIDE Master: Needs a 2300 rating, and it is usually earned by players who are already well known on the national tournament circuit.
Chess ratings: titles and peaks.International Master: This title requires norms, strong tournament performances against titled opponents, as well as the 2400 rating.
Chess ratings: titles and peaks.Grandmaster: The highest standard title, and Bobby Fischer earned it at 15 in 1958, making him the youngest grandmaster at that time.
Chess ratings: titles and peaks.The super-GM club: Only a small elite of players have ever passed 2700, and the top handful of the world's players are usually found here.
Chess ratings: titles and peaks.Bobby Fischer's peak: He reached it just before beating Boris Spassky in Reykjavik in 1972, ending decades of Soviet dominance of the world title.
Chess ratings: titles and peaks.Garry Kasparov's peak: His 2851 in 1999 stood as the record for 14 years, until his eventual successor, Magnus Carlsen, passed it.
Chess ratings: titles and peaks.Magnus Carlsen's peak: The highest rating ever, 2882 in 2014, reached by the Norwegian, who became a grandmaster at only 13.

African capitals from north to south.Tunis: Close to the ruins of ancient Carthage, Tunis has a UNESCO-listed medina and is the northernmost capital on the African continent.
African capitals from north to south.Rabat: Morocco's capital, not Casablanca or Marrakech; its Hassan Tower is the stump of a mosque minaret that was never finished.
African capitals from north to south.Cairo: The Giza pyramids stand on the edge of its sprawl, and the metropolitan area holds over 20 million people, among Africa's largest.
African capitals from north to south.Dakar: Sitting on Cap-Vert, near the westernmost tip of mainland Africa, it once ended the Dakar Rally, which now races in Saudi Arabia.
African capitals from north to south.Addis Ababa: The name means 'new flower' in Amharic; at about 2,300 metres it is among the highest capitals anywhere, and it hosts the African Union.
African capitals from north to south.Accra: The capital of Ghana, the first sub-Saharan colony to win independence, in 1957, under Kwame Nkrumah.
African capitals from north to south.Kinshasa: It sits across the Congo River from Brazzaville, and these two are among the closest pair of national capitals in the world.
African capitals from north to south.Luanda: Founded by the Portuguese in 1576, Angola's capital has several times been ranked among the priciest cities for expatriates.
African capitals from north to south.Lusaka: Zambia's capital stands about 1,280 metres above sea level, which keeps it noticeably cooler than its latitude suggests.
African capitals from north to south.Pretoria: One of South Africa's three capitals, the executive one, and in October thousands of jacaranda trees turn its streets purple.

Colors your eyes see, by wavelength.Ultraviolet (invisible): Bees see it and many flowers carry hidden ultraviolet patterns that guide them to nectar, while our eye's lens blocks most of it.
Colors your eyes see, by wavelength.Violet: A spectral colour, unlike purple, which is just a mix of red and blue light that has no wavelength of its own.
Colors your eyes see, by wavelength.Indigo: Newton added it to make seven colours, to match the notes of the musical scale, though many people struggle to see it.
Colors your eyes see, by wavelength.Blue: The sky looks this way because air molecules scatter shorter wavelengths more strongly, an effect called Rayleigh scattering.
Colors your eyes see, by wavelength.Cyan: The C of CMYK printing, this greenish-blue ink is mixed with magenta, yellow and black to produce almost every colour you see.
Colors your eyes see, by wavelength.Green: Human eyes are most sensitive to this wavelength in daylight, which is why night-vision displays and safety vests favour it.
Colors your eyes see, by wavelength.Yellow: Screens make it by mixing red and green light, so no yellow light is needed, and your eye cannot tell the difference.
Colors your eyes see, by wavelength.Orange: English had no word for this colour until the fruit arrived, and it was earlier described as yellow-red.
Colors your eyes see, by wavelength.Red: This is the longest wavelength we see, and sunsets turn this colour because it scatters the least on the way through air.
Colors your eyes see, by wavelength.Infrared (invisible): Pit vipers sense it through special organs, and remote controls use it, which is why a phone camera can reveal their flash.

Distance from Los Angeles.San Diego: Home to the US Pacific Fleet, it neighbors Tijuana, and the San Ysidro crossing is the busiest land border crossing in the Western Hemisphere.
Distance from Los Angeles.Las Vegas: A huge share of its visitors drive from Los Angeles, and the Strip actually sits outside the city limits, in unincorporated Paradise.
Distance from Los Angeles.San Francisco: The northern rival was the largest city on the West Coast until the 1920 census, when Los Angeles overtook it.
Distance from Los Angeles.Seattle: Boeing's early home and the birthplace of Starbucks and Amazon; it gets less annual rain than New York.
Distance from Los Angeles.Mexico City: It stands on the drained bed of Lake Texcoco, atop the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan, and parts of the city are sinking.
Distance from Los Angeles.Chicago: Route 66 began here and ended in Santa Monica, near Los Angeles, a roughly 3,900 km journey.
Distance from Los Angeles.Miami: The name likely comes from the Mayaimi people, and the city was incorporated in 1896, later becoming the cruise capital of the world.
Distance from Los Angeles.Honolulu: Reached from the mainland only by sea or air, the flight takes about five and a half hours.
Distance from Los Angeles.London: Flights take about eleven hours, and the clocks differ by eight hours.
Distance from Los Angeles.Sydney: Flying west, you cross the International Date Line and land about two calendar days after you left.

Ancient and medieval classics, by date.Epic of Gilgamesh: Gilgamesh, king of Uruk, seeks immortality, and the poem includes a flood story that predates Noah's by many centuries.
Ancient and medieval classics, by date.The Iliad: Homer's epic covers only a few weeks of the Trojan War, centered on Achilles's rage; the wooden horse isn't even in it.
Ancient and medieval classics, by date.Oedipus Rex: Sophocles's play has Oedipus unknowingly fulfil a terrible prophecy, and Aristotle held it up as a model tragedy.
Ancient and medieval classics, by date.The Aeneid: Virgil reportedly asked for it to be burned on his deathbed, but Augustus saved it; it traces Rome's roots to Trojan hero Aeneas.
Ancient and medieval classics, by date.Ovid's Metamorphoses: Ovid's poem retells some 250 myths of transformation, and became a rich source for Shakespeare and countless painters.
Ancient and medieval classics, by date.Beowulf: The longest surviving Old English epic, it exists in a single manuscript that was scorched in a 1731 library fire.
Ancient and medieval classics, by date.The Tale of Genji: Written by the court lady Murasaki Shikibu, it is often called the world's first novel.
Ancient and medieval classics, by date.The Divine Comedy: Dante journeys through Hell, Purgatory and Paradise, writing in Italian rather than Latin, which helped shape the literary language.
Ancient and medieval classics, by date.The Decameron: Ten young people flee plague-stricken Florence and tell 100 tales; Boccaccio wrote it after the Black Death of 1348.
Ancient and medieval classics, by date.The Canterbury Tales: Chaucer's pilgrims tell stories on the road to Canterbury; he left it unfinished, with 24 tales done of a planned 120 or so.

When these countries ended their monarch.Brazil: Emperor Pedro II was deposed in a largely bloodless military coup in 1889. He died in exile in Paris.
When these countries ended their monarch.Hawaii: Queen Liliuokalani was overthrown by American-backed businessmen in 1893, and the islands were annexed by the US five years later.
When these countries ended their monarch.Portugal: A revolution ended a monarchy of roughly 800 years in 1910, and King Manuel II fled to Britain.
When these countries ended their monarch.Germany: Kaiser Wilhelm II abdicated as WWI collapsed, and the new Weimar Republic was declared from a balcony of the Reichstag.
When these countries ended their monarch.Italy: A 1946 referendum ended the monarchy, and King Umberto II had reigned only about a month, earning the nickname 'the May King'.
When these countries ended their monarch.Egypt: After the 1952 coup forced King Farouk out, the republic was formally declared the following year.
When these countries ended their monarch.Iraq: King Faisal II, aged 23, was killed in the 1958 coup that made Iraq a republic.
When these countries ended their monarch.Greece: The ruling junta abolished the monarchy in 1973, and a 1974 referendum confirmed it, with roughly two thirds voting against the king.
When these countries ended their monarch.Iran: The Shah fled in early 1979, ending a monarchy that traced its roots back thousands of years, and the Islamic Republic followed.
When these countries ended their monarch.Nepal: In 2008 a new assembly voted to abolish a kingdom that had existed since 1768 and Nepal became a republic.

Famous meteorites and when they turned u.Ensisheim (France): The Ensisheim stone fell in 1492 and was chained in a church, as people took it for a sign from heaven. It is the oldest meteorite with a witnessed fall in Europe.
Famous meteorites and when they turned u.Willamette (found): Willamette is the largest meteorite found in the United States, about 15 tons; it was long sacred to the Clackamas people, who used its pits to collect rainwater.
Famous meteorites and when they turned u.Tunguska event: A mid-air blast flattened some 80 million trees over roughly 2,000 square kilometres of Siberia, yet left no crater. It was probably a disintegrating space rock.
Famous meteorites and when they turned u.Nakhla (Mars rock, Egypt): A fragment of this Martian rock reportedly killed a dog in Egypt, though the tale is doubtful. It is famous for showing that water once altered the rock on Mars.
Famous meteorites and when they turned u.Hoba (found, Namibia): Hoba is the largest known intact meteorite, around 60 tons of iron and nickel. It lies where it fell, since it was too heavy to move.
Famous meteorites and when they turned u.Sikhote-Alin (Russia): A spectacular iron shower broke into thousands of pieces over Siberia, and the biggest left over 100 craters in the snowy forest.
Famous meteorites and when they turned u.Sylacauga (hit a woman): Ann Hodges was napping on her sofa when a grapefruit-sized stone crashed through her roof and bruised her. She is the only well-documented person struck by a meteorite.
Famous meteorites and when they turned u.Allende (Mexico): This carbonaceous chondrite broke into tonnes of fragments over Chihuahua, and it holds some of the oldest solid matter in our solar system, older than the Earth.
Famous meteorites and when they turned u.Peekskill (hit a car): A Chevrolet Malibu was dented by a 12-kilogram meteorite in New York. The car later sold for far more than it was worth, and the rock was named after it.
Famous meteorites and when they turned u.Chelyabinsk: A bright fireball exploded over Russia's Urals, and its shockwave shattered windows across Chelyabinsk. It was the largest such object recorded in over a century.

TV news and talk institutions by debut.Today: It is NBC's morning show, and it was the first to launch the breakfast news genre, with a chimpanzee named J. Fred Muggs as a mascot.
TV news and talk institutions by debut.The Tonight Show: It is the longest-running talk show in the world, and its hosts have included Johnny Carson, who held the job for 30 years.
TV news and talk institutions by debut.60 Minutes: This investigative news show is known for its ticking stopwatch and it was the first TV news magazine program.
TV news and talk institutions by debut.Saturday Night Live: Sketch show created by Lorne Michaels, which began as a live show in a New York studio, and it launched a generation of comedians.
TV news and talk institutions by debut.Late Night with Letterman: David Letterman's late-night show was known for its irreverent humour, including Top Ten lists and stupid pet tricks.
TV news and talk institutions by debut.The Oprah Winfrey Show: She became the first TV host to reach a billion dollars in wealth, and her book club made reading fashionable.
TV news and talk institutions by debut.The Daily Show: The satirical news show was hosted by Jon Stewart, and it gave rise to many stars including Stephen Colbert and John Oliver.
TV news and talk institutions by debut.The Ellen DeGeneres Show: The syndicated daytime talk show ran for 19 seasons, and it was known for giveaways and dance openings.
TV news and talk institutions by debut.The Colbert Report: Stephen Colbert played a fictional right-wing pundit on this show, and it was a spin-off of The Daily Show.
TV news and talk institutions by debut.Last Week Tonight: John Oliver's HBO show features long investigations of public issues, and it won many Emmy awards.

When these board games came out.Monopoly: It grew from Lizzie Magie's 1904 Landlord's Game, which was designed to show how landlords enrich themselves at everyone else's cost.
When these board games came out.Scrabble: Out-of-work architect Alfred Butts invented it in the Depression, and first called it Lexiko, then Criss-Crosswords.
When these board games came out.Cluedo: Anthony Pratt, a musician and solicitor's clerk, conceived it during wartime blackouts. Americans know it as Clue.
When these board games came out.Mouse Trap: Its elaborate contraption, built piece by piece, echoes the chain-reaction machines drawn by cartoonist Rube Goldberg.
When these board games came out.Operation: University student John Spinello designed it, and reportedly sold the idea for just 500 dollars.
When these board games came out.Twister: It got a huge boost when Johnny Carson and Eva Gabor played it on The Tonight Show in 1966.
When these board games came out.Hungry Hungry Hippos: Milton Bradley's marble-chomping game needs no reading and no strategy, so preschoolers can beat their parents.
When these board games came out.Jenga: Leslie Scott, who grew up partly in Africa, named it from the Swahili word 'kujenga', meaning 'to build'.
When these board games came out.Catan: Klaus Teuber, a dental technician, created it, and its success helped start the boom in German-style board games.
When these board games came out.Cards Against Humanity: Friends crowdfunded it on Kickstarter, and later sold nothing on Black Friday as a stunt, taking in tens of thousands of dollars.

Airship history, by year.Zeppelin LZ 1 first flight: Count Ferdinand von Zeppelin's first airship flew over Lake Constance, with a rigid aluminum frame inside the fabric skin.
Airship history, by year.USS Shenandoah first flight: The first US rigid airship used helium, not hydrogen, and was torn apart in a storm over Ohio in 1925.
Airship history, by year.Goodyear's first blimp: Pilgrim was Goodyear's first blimp; later blimps became famous as flying advertisements and TV camera platforms.
Airship history, by year.Norge flies over North Pole: Roald Amundsen, Lincoln Ellsworth and Umberto Nobile flew it from Spitsbergen to Alaska, the first undisputed flight over the North Pole.
Airship history, by year.Graf Zeppelin first flight: It flew around the world in 1929 in about three weeks, and carried passengers on over 500 flights without injury.
Airship history, by year.R101 crashes in France: The R101 crashed in France on its way to India, killing 48 of 54 aboard, which ended British airship ambitions.
Airship history, by year.USS Akron first flight: This US Navy airship carried fighter planes in its belly, a flying aircraft carrier; it crashed in a storm in 1933, killing 73.
Airship history, by year.Hindenburg disaster: A hydrogen fire at Lakehurst, New Jersey, killed 36 people, and the filmed disaster ended the age of passenger airships.
Airship history, by year.Zeppelin NT first flight: This modern semi-rigid design uses helium and still gives sightseeing flights, notably over Lake Constance.
Airship history, by year.Airlander 10 first flight: At about 92 m it was once the world's longest aircraft, nicknamed the Flying Bum for its twin-lobed shape.

States vs. nations: who's bigger?.Rhode Island: Its official name was 'State of Rhode Island and Providence Plantations' until voters dropped the second half in 2020.
States vs. nations: who's bigger?.Ireland: The Republic of Ireland has no native snakes, which legend credits to St Patrick.
States vs. nations: who's bigger?.Florida: It has the longest coastline of the contiguous states.
States vs. nations: who's bigger?.United Kingdom: England alone makes up more than half of the UK's area.
States vs. nations: who's bigger?.Germany: It borders nine countries, more than any other in Europe.
States vs. nations: who's bigger?.California: If it were its own country, its economy would be larger than almost all nations'.
States vs. nations: who's bigger?.France: The area shown includes overseas regions such as French Guiana. Mainland France covers about 550,000 square kilometres.
States vs. nations: who's bigger?.Texas: Was an independent republic from 1836 until joining the United States in 1845.
States vs. nations: who's bigger?.Alaska: Bought from Russia in 1867 for $7.2 million, it is more than twice as big as Texas.
States vs. nations: who's bigger?.Mexico: Mexico City stands on the lake bed of the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan. Mexico has the most Spanish speakers of any country.

Number of possible outcomes.Coin flip: Real coins can land on their edge, about once in 6,000 flips for a nickel.
Number of possible outcomes.Rock-paper-scissors throw: Played in organized championships around the world.
Number of possible outcomes.Tetrahedral die: The four-sided die lands on a point, so you read the number on the top or bottom, and it is notorious for hurting bare feet.
Number of possible outcomes.Standard cube die: The faces on opposite sides always add up to seven.
Number of possible outcomes.Octahedral die: Each face is a triangle, and it shows up in tabletop games.
Number of possible outcomes.Dodecahedral die: Twelve pentagonal faces make this one of the five Platonic solids.
Number of possible outcomes.Icosahedral die: The d20 is the signature die of Dungeons and Dragons.
Number of possible outcomes.Rolling two dice (ordered): There are 36 ordered results but only 11 totals, and 7 is the most likely, with six ways to make it.
Number of possible outcomes.European roulette spin: European roulette has 37 pockets, 0 to 36. The American wheel adds a double zero for 38.
Number of possible outcomes.Drawing from a deck of cards: A shuffled deck can be ordered in about 8 followed by 67 zeros ways, so every well-shuffled deck is almost certainly unique.

Stars by size (radius).Sirius B (white dwarf): A white dwarf about Earth's size but about as massive as the Sun, so it is incredibly dense.
Stars by size (radius).Proxima Centauri: The nearest star to the Sun is a red dwarf too faint to see with the naked eye.
Stars by size (radius).The Sun: It holds about 99.8 percent of the solar system's mass.
Stars by size (radius).Sirius A: The brightest star in our night sky, part of a pair with a white dwarf companion.
Stars by size (radius).Vega: It was our northern pole star around 12,000 BC and will be again in about 12,000 years.
Stars by size (radius).Arcturus: An orange giant, the brightest star in the northern celestial hemisphere.
Stars by size (radius).Aldebaran: An orange giant marking the bull's eye in Taurus.
Stars by size (radius).Rigel: A blue supergiant marking Orion's foot, and tens of thousands of times as luminous as the Sun.
Stars by size (radius).Betelgeuse: This red supergiant would reach past Mars if placed at the Sun, and it will eventually explode as a supernova.
Stars by size (radius).VY Canis Majoris: One of the biggest known stars, though estimates of its size have been revised over the years.

Great horse races, by first running.St Leger Stakes: Named for Anthony St Leger, it's run at Doncaster, is the oldest of Britain's five Classics, and ends the Triple Crown.
Great horse races, by first running.Grand National: Run at Aintree over huge fences, it is a test of stamina, and it's watched by hundreds of millions worldwide.
Great horse races, by first running.Melbourne Cup: It's called 'the race that stops a nation', and Melbourne holds a public holiday for it on the first Tuesday of November.
Great horse races, by first running.Belmont Stakes: Run in New York, it's the final leg of the American Triple Crown and nicknamed the 'Test of the Champion'.
Great horse races, by first running.Preakness Stakes: The middle jewel of the Triple Crown, it is known for the black-eyed Susans draped over the winner.
Great horse races, by first running.Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe: Run at Longchamp, it is Europe's richest turf race, and Paris hosts it every October.
Great horse races, by first running.Cheltenham Gold Cup: The top prize in National Hunt jump racing, it's held at Cheltenham each March, with Irish fans crossing the sea in thousands.
Great horse races, by first running.Japan Cup: Created to bring top international runners to Japan, it's run at Tokyo's Fuchu racecourse, and it's among the world's richest turf races.
Great horse races, by first running.Breeders' Cup: Held on a different US track each year, it packs a whole season's championship races into two days of top-class action.
Great horse races, by first running.Dubai World Cup: Run at the Meydan racecourse, it's famous for the richest purse in horse racing, once reaching 12 million dollars.

When these things named after people app.The sandwich: The Earl of Sandwich is said to have eaten meat between bread so he wouldn't have to leave a card game.
When these things named after people app.The guillotine: Dr Joseph-Ignace Guillotin proposed the machine as a humane form of execution, though he personally opposed the death penalty.
When these things named after people app.Braille: Louis Braille was blind from a childhood accident and developed his reading system as a teenager, inspired by an army code.
When these things named after people app.The saxophone: Adolphe Sax, a Belgian instrument maker, patented his brass-and-reed hybrid in Paris, and survived several near-death accidents in his life.
When these things named after people app.The Ferris wheel: George Ferris built his giant wheel for the 1893 Chicago World's Fair as an answer to the Eiffel Tower.
When these things named after people app.The Zeppelin: Count Ferdinand von Zeppelin pioneered rigid airships, and the first one took flight in 1900 over Lake Constance.
When these things named after people app.The teddy bear: Theodore Roosevelt refused to shoot a tied-up bear on a hunt, and a cartoon of it inspired toymakers to name the plush toy after him.
When these things named after people app.The Biro pen: Hungarian journalist Laszlo Biro patented a ballpoint pen with fast-drying ink, inspired by newspaper printing ink.
When these things named after people app.The Jacuzzi tub: Candido Jacuzzi's family first made whirlpool pumps to treat his son's arthritis, and the tub became a luxury item.
When these things named after people app.The Rubik's Cube: Hungarian architect Erno Rubik built it as a teaching tool for 3D geometry, and over 350 million have been sold.

Japanese arts and letters, through histo.Kojiki (chronicle): Compiled at the imperial court, Japan's oldest surviving book recounts creation myths and the divine origins of the imperial line.
Japanese arts and letters, through histo.The Tale of Genji: Written by court lady Murasaki Shikibu, it is often called the world's first novel, following the romantic life of Prince Genji.
Japanese arts and letters, through histo.Hōjōki: Kamo no Chōmei wrote it as a hermit in a tiny hut after fires, quakes and famine, reflecting on how impermanent all things are.
Japanese arts and letters, through histo.Zeami's Noh treatise: Zeami, the great master of Noh theatre, wrote treatises on acting, including the idea of the 'flower', the quality that captivates an audience.
Japanese arts and letters, through histo.Kabuki is born: A shrine maiden named Izumo no Okuni is credited with starting it in Kyoto; women were later banned and men played every role.
Japanese arts and letters, through histo.Bashō's Narrow Road: Bashō's travel diary mixes prose and haiku on a months-long walk through northern Japan, and is a masterpiece of the form.
Japanese arts and letters, through histo.The Great Wave: Hokusai's woodblock print shows a towering wave dwarfing fishing boats, with Mount Fuji small behind; it inspired many Western artists.
Japanese arts and letters, through histo.Sōseki's I Am a Cat: Natsume Sōseki's debut novel is narrated by a nameless house cat who wryly observes his owner's circle of friends.
Japanese arts and letters, through histo.Sōseki's Kokoro: This Sōseki novel's title means 'heart'; it follows a student and his troubled teacher and remains one of Japan's best-selling books.
Japanese arts and letters, through histo.Murakami's Norwegian Wood: Named after a Beatles song, Murakami's novel of love and loss in 1960s Tokyo made him a literary star in Japan.

Dinosaurs from nose to tail.Compsognathus: One of the smallest known non-avian dinosaurs, about the size of a turkey, found in Germany.
Dinosaurs from nose to tail.Velociraptor: Despite the movies, it was turkey-sized and feathered; its name means 'swift thief'.
Dinosaurs from nose to tail.Deinonychus: Studying it in the 1960s led John Ostrom to argue that birds descend from dinosaurs.
Dinosaurs from nose to tail.Pachycephalosaurus: Its name means 'thick-headed lizard', for a domed skull that could be many centimetres thick.
Dinosaurs from nose to tail.Dilophosaurus: Jurassic Park invented its venom spit and neck frill; the real animal had two crests on its skull.
Dinosaurs from nose to tail.Triceratops: Its huge skull and horns may have been used for combat and display.
Dinosaurs from nose to tail.Tyrannosaurus rex: Its bite was among the strongest of any land animal, and its tiny arms were surprisingly powerful.
Dinosaurs from nose to tail.Spinosaurus: Possibly the biggest meat-eating dinosaur, it had a sail on its back and likely hunted fish.
Dinosaurs from nose to tail.Diplodocus: Its whip-like tail was about half its length, and Andrew Carnegie donated casts to museums around the world.
Dinosaurs from nose to tail.Argentinosaurus: This Argentine titanosaur may have weighed 70 tonnes, though estimates vary since it's known from fragments.

How many of each aircraft were built.Antonov An-225: Only one An-225 Mriya was ever completed; the world's largest aircraft was destroyed in 2022 at Hostomel airport near Kyiv.
How many of each aircraft were built.Concorde: Only 20 Concordes were built, and they crossed the Atlantic in under three and a half hours at twice the speed of sound.
How many of each aircraft were built.SR-71 Blackbird: The SR-71 flew at over Mach 3 and still holds speed records; its skin leaked fuel on the ground until it heated up in flight.
How many of each aircraft were built.Boeing 747: The 747 was the first 'jumbo jet', and its distinctive upper deck hump was designed so it could be converted to a freighter.
How many of each aircraft were built.Douglas DC-3 and C-47: Called the Gooney Bird, the DC-3 is so durable that hundreds still fly today, nearly a century after the design first flew.
How many of each aircraft were built.B-24 Liberator: The Liberator was built in greater numbers than any other American military aircraft, partly thanks to Ford's Willow Run assembly line.
How many of each aircraft were built.Supermarine Spitfire: The Spitfire's elliptical wing and Rolls-Royce Merlin engine made it a symbol of Britain's defense in the Battle of Britain.
How many of each aircraft were built.Messerschmitt Bf 109: Willy Messerschmitt's Bf 109 was Germany's main fighter, built in more numbers than any other fighter in history.
How many of each aircraft were built.Ilyushin Il-2 Shturmovik: Called the 'flying tank', the Il-2 was an armored ground-attack plane, and it was among the most-produced military aircraft ever.
How many of each aircraft were built.Cessna 172: The Cessna 172 first flew in 1955 and is the most-produced aircraft ever, and generations of pilots learned to fly in it.

German inventions and discoveries.Gutenberg press: Johannes Gutenberg's movable-type press made books cheap to produce. His 42-line Bible is among Europe's first major printed books.
German inventions and discoveries.Henlein's pocket watch: The Nuremberg locksmith Peter Henlein is credited with early portable clocks, nicknamed 'Nuremberg eggs', though the story is debated.
German inventions and discoveries.Bunsen burner: Developed from Robert Bunsen's lab design by his assistant Peter Desaga. Its adjustable air intake gives a hot, clean flame.
German inventions and discoveries.Benz motor car: Karl Benz's three-wheeler is widely seen as the first practical car. His wife Bertha made history's first long road trip in one.
German inventions and discoveries.X-rays (Röntgen): Wilhelm Röntgen found them by accident. His first image was of his wife's hand, ring included, and he won the first Physics Nobel.
German inventions and discoveries.Aspirin (Bayer): Chemist Felix Hoffmann at Bayer made a usable form of acetylsalicylic acid, a compound known from willow bark.
German inventions and discoveries.Zeppelin airship: Count Ferdinand von Zeppelin's rigid airships flew passengers across the Atlantic until the Hindenburg burned in 1937.
German inventions and discoveries.Melitta coffee filter: Melitta Bentz punched holes in a brass pot and lined it with blotting paper from her son's school notebook. Her company still bears her name.
German inventions and discoveries.Haribo gummy bears: Hans Riegel of Bonn founded the firm. The name is HAns RIegel BOnn. His first sweet was a dancing bear.
German inventions and discoveries.Heinkel jet plane: The He 178 made the first jet-powered flight, days before World War II began, beating Britain's jet by about two years.

Rulers of France from Henry IV to Napole.Henry IV: The first Bourbon king, who reportedly said 'Paris is worth a Mass' when converting to Catholicism. He was assassinated in 1610.
Rulers of France from Henry IV to Napole.Louis XIII: He took the throne at eight, and Cardinal Richelieu largely ran the country. The Three Musketeers is set in his reign.
Rulers of France from Henry IV to Napole.Louis XIV: The Sun King reigned for 72 years, the longest of any major European monarch, and built Versailles.
Rulers of France from Henry IV to Napole.Louis XV: Succeeded his great-grandfather at age five. His reign saw France lose much of its American empire.
Rulers of France from Henry IV to Napole.Louis XVI: Beheaded by guillotine in 1793 during the French Revolution.
Rulers of France from Henry IV to Napole.Napoleon I: Crowned himself emperor in 1804. At about 1.68 m, he was of average height for his time.
Rulers of France from Henry IV to Napole.Louis XVIII: Took the throne after years in exile, following Napoleon's downfall.
Rulers of France from Henry IV to Napole.Charles X: The last Bourbon king, overthrown in the July Revolution of 1830.
Rulers of France from Henry IV to Napole.Louis-Philippe: The 'Citizen King', known for his bourgeois style, including carrying an umbrella; overthrown in 1848.
Rulers of France from Henry IV to Napole.Napoleon III: A nephew of Napoleon, he was France's first popularly elected president and was captured at Sedan in 1870.

Byzantium, in chronological order.Constantinople dedicated: Emperor Constantine rededicated the city of Byzantium and called it the 'New Rome', but it soon took his name.
Byzantium, in chronological order.Theodosian Walls built: Built in 413 under Theodosius II, they stood as a triple line of defenses and held off attackers for a thousand years.
Byzantium, in chronological order.Hagia Sophia completed: Justinian's builders finished it in under six years, with a dome that seems to float.
Byzantium, in chronological order.First Arab siege: The Byzantines repelled the Arab fleet with 'Greek fire', a secret burning liquid that even floated on water.
Byzantium, in chronological order.Iconoclasm begins: Emperor Leo III banned the veneration of religious images, beginning decades of conflict over icons.
Byzantium, in chronological order.Basil II wins at Kleidion: His victory over the Bulgarians earned Basil II the nickname 'Bulgar-Slayer'.
Byzantium, in chronological order.Great Schism: Rome and Constantinople excommunicated each other in 1054, a break that was formally lifted only in 1965.
Byzantium, in chronological order.Battle of Manzikert: Seljuk Turks captured Emperor Romanos IV, opening Anatolia to Turkish settlement.
Byzantium, in chronological order.Byzantines retake the city: Michael VIII Palaiologos took it back from the Latin rulers who had held it since the Fourth Crusade's 1204 sack.
Byzantium, in chronological order.Fall to the Ottomans: Mehmed II's huge cannons breached the walls on 29 May 1453, and the last emperor, Constantine XI, died fighting.

How much these squirrel relatives weigh.African pygmy squirrel: One of the world's smallest squirrels, it lives in Central African rainforests and weighs less than a AA battery.
How much these squirrel relatives weigh.Least chipmunk: The smallest chipmunk in North America, it lives in habitats from deserts to mountain meadows.
How much these squirrel relatives weigh.Southern flying squirrel: It does not truly fly but glides on a skin membrane between its limbs, and its fur glows pink under ultraviolet light.
How much these squirrel relatives weigh.Eastern chipmunk: Its cheek pouches stretch to carry a mass of seeds, and it digs burrows with hidden, tidy entrances.
How much these squirrel relatives weigh.Red squirrel: In Britain, native red squirrels have been largely replaced by introduced grays, partly because grays carry squirrelpox virus.
How much these squirrel relatives weigh.Eastern gray squirrel: It buries thousands of nuts each autumn and forgets many, which helps grow new oak trees.
How much these squirrel relatives weigh.Black-tailed prairie dog: Their burrow colonies are called towns, and researchers say their alarm calls can describe a predator's size and colour.
How much these squirrel relatives weigh.Indian giant squirrel: A colourful tree-dweller from India, also called the Malabar giant squirrel, and the state animal of Maharashtra.
How much these squirrel relatives weigh.Woodchuck: Also called a groundhog, it is the star of Groundhog Day, and truly hibernates, with its heartbeat slowing to a few beats a minute.
How much these squirrel relatives weigh.Hoary marmot: One of the largest squirrel relatives, it whistles warnings, which gave Whistler mountain in Canada its name.

Jewish history, in dates.First Temple destroyed: Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon destroyed Solomon's Temple and exiled many Judeans to Babylon.
Jewish history, in dates.Second Temple dedicated: Exiles returning from Babylon rebuilt the temple after the Persian king Cyrus allowed it.
Jewish history, in dates.Maccabean revolt begins: Judah Maccabee led a revolt against Seleucid rule, and Hanukkah commemorates the rededication of the Temple.
Jewish history, in dates.Second Temple destroyed: Roman legions under Titus burned the temple, and the Western Wall is a remnant of its supporting wall.
Jewish history, in dates.Bar Kokhba revolt: After its defeat, Emperor Hadrian renamed Judea Syria Palaestina, and Simon bar Kokhba's name became a symbol of resistance.
Jewish history, in dates.Expulsion from Spain: The Alhambra Decree gave Jews months to convert or leave; many resettled in Ottoman lands and Portugal.
Jewish history, in dates.Dreyfus affair begins: A French Jewish army officer was falsely convicted of treason; Emile Zola's J'accuse defended him, and the affair inspired Herzl.
Jewish history, in dates.Balfour Declaration: A letter of under 70 words from Arthur Balfour promised support for a national home for the Jewish people.
Jewish history, in dates.State of Israel founded: David Ben-Gurion declared independence in Tel Aviv on 14 May.
Jewish history, in dates.Jerusalem reunified: During the Six-Day War, Israeli forces took the Old City, including the Western Wall.

Books of the Hebrew Bible, in order.Genesis: The name means 'origin' in Greek, while the Hebrew title Bereshit is simply its opening word, 'in the beginning'.
Books of the Hebrew Bible, in order.Exodus: This book tells of the escape from Egypt and the giving of the Ten Commandments at Sinai.
Books of the Hebrew Bible, in order.Leviticus: Named for the tribe of Levi, the priests' tribe, it covers laws of sacrifice and purity, and contains 'love your neighbor as yourself'.
Books of the Hebrew Bible, in order.Numbers: Its name comes from two censuses of the Israelites, though the Hebrew title Bamidbar means 'in the wilderness'.
Books of the Hebrew Bible, in order.Deuteronomy: Its name means 'second law' in Greek, and the book consists largely of Moses's farewell speeches before he dies.
Books of the Hebrew Bible, in order.Joshua: The first book of the Prophets recounts the conquest of Canaan, including the famous fall of Jericho's walls.
Books of the Hebrew Bible, in order.Judges: This book features figures like Deborah and Samson, who led Israel in the era before it had kings.
Books of the Hebrew Bible, in order.Samuel: Originally a single book, it was split into two in translation, and it tells of Saul and David's rise to kingship.
Books of the Hebrew Bible, in order.Kings: It follows the monarchy from Solomon's Temple to the Babylonian exile, and originally was one book, later divided in two.
Books of the Hebrew Bible, in order.Isaiah: The first of the Latter Prophets, it contains the vision of swords beaten into plowshares, a line later inscribed at the UN.
